title: Predictive Burst Absorption and Graceful Limiter Hibernation
creator: Aisha Turner
description: Problem: During transient traffic spikes and cross-region failovers we observe asymmetric latency and token loss due to aggressive hard caps and slow rehydration of limiter state. Existing mitigations (soft credits and emergency spillover) reduce outages but create oscillations and temporary unfairness between tenants.
goals: 1) Add a predictive soft-credit allocator (Predictive Burst Absorber) that pre-allocates transient capacity based on short-term EWMA demand forecasts and historical burst profiles. 2) Implement a graceful limiter hibernation mode that drains non-critical state and converts replicas to standby under sustained low-utilization to reduce outage blast radius when a primary limiter fails. 3) Preserve tenant fairness (proportional deficit accounting) during pre-allocation and hibernation transitions. 4) Provide rollout and telemetry that ties directly to SLOs and multi-region failover playbooks.
acceptance_criteria:
- Predictive allocator reduces observed 95th-percentile rejected requests during synthetic bursts by >=50% in staging benchmark relative to baseline.
- Hibernation mode enables fast failover with limiter replica cold-start time < 120s and no more than 5% increase in 99th-percentile latency for P0 tenants during failover.
- Fairness invariants preserved: long-running tenants should not lose more than their proportional share during pre-allocation events.
- Dashboards and alerts added: predictive-credit-utilization, hibernation-transitions, and fairness-degradation.
- End-to-end e2e chaos test (region partition + limiter restart) in CI that asserts application-level SLOs remain within guardrails.
design_notes:
- Predictive Burst Absorber will run as a sidecar service within limiter clusters that samples request rate per tenant and uses a short-horizon EWMA + seasonality detector to suggest soft-credit windows.
- Pre-allocated credits are tagged with TTL and an origin tag to allow safe reclaiming; eviction uses proportional deficit accounting to minimize fairness drift.
- Hibernation transitions: NORMAL -> PREPARE (reduce commit window and replicate minimal state to standby) -> HIBERNATE (drop heavy caches, switch to minimized admission controller) -> RESTORE. Each transition emits structured events to tracing and an audit log.
- Interactions with circuit breakers: when the panic circuit trips in a region, the hibernation protocol will attempt to move replicas to remote regions using the routing layer and consult cross-region capacity hints to avoid double-counting credits.
- Telemetry: add sampling for denied request traces, credit-origin histogram, eviction-reason counters, and transition duration histograms.
- Backwards compatibility: fall back to current soft-credit behavior if predictive sidecar is unavailable.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): build sidecar prototype, wire sampling, and local EWMA forecasting. Phase 2 (2 weeks): safe pre-allocation API, TTL semantics, eviction policy, and unit tests. Phase 3 (2 weeks): hibernation protocol implementation and state-minimization paths. Phase 4 (1 week): staging benchmarks and fairness simulator. Phase 5 (1 week): rollout with feature flag by region and canary on low-traffic tenants. Phase 6: run chaos and SLO gating before full rollout.
testing_and_telemetry:
- Synthetic burst harness that can replay production ingress patterns per-tenant.
- Fairness simulator that compares proportional deficit accounting against naive pre-allocation.
- Integration tests for state replication and hibernation transition events.
- Grafana dashboards and PagerDuty runbook entries for hibernation anomalies.
- CI job that runs region partition + limiter restart scenario; job must assert application SLOs (p99 latency and error budget consumption) below threshold.
rollout_strategy: Start with a feature-flagged canary in us-west with test tenants only. After 48h and no major regressions, expand to 10% of production traffic and monitor fairness and denied-rate deltas. Use automatic rollback if denied-rate for P0 customers increases by >2x or p99 latency increases >15% relative to baseline. Coordinate with Traffic Routing and Runbook teams for failover windows.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Forecast over-allocates credits causing capacity exhaustion. Mitigation: hard global cap and conservative multiplier with decay; circuit breaker to disable predictive allocator if cluster headroom < threshold.
- Risk: Hibernation increases restore latency. Mitigation: staged warmup of standby replicas and persistent minimal KV snapshot.
- Risk: Complexity in multi-region accounting. Mitigation: add a reconciliation worker that runs periodically to correct cross-region credit drift and emit reconciliation diff metrics.
open_questions:
- What threshold for predictive headroom is acceptable before we disable pre-allocation? Proposal: 15% headroom.
- Do we need KMS approval for storing TTL-tagged credit origin info in the audit log? (security asked)
- Should hibernated replicas maintain a tiny KV snapshot for faster restore or rely on warmup traffic? Decision deferred to ops after staging results.
